title: Assembly and naturality of the constant-ring isomorphism
statement: Let (C,JC),(D,JD) be small sites with commutative-ring sheafification, L a finite-limit-preserving set-sheaf functor, rings a functor of commutative-ring sheaves, and e_R:L(|R|)≅|rings(R)| natural in R and compatible with all four ring-operation graphs. Suppose κ:constant_C ⋙ L ≅ constant_D is natural in all sets [lem-route-inverse-image-constant-set-comparison]. There is an isomorphism constants:constant_C ⋙ rings ≅ constant_D of commutative-ring-sheaf functors whose underlying component at A is e_{constant_C A}^{-1} followed by the conjugated set comparison. Unlike the parent theorem, this statement takes κ as input and makes no constant-section normalization assertion.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: For each A define f_A=e_{constant_C A}^{-1};κ_A^ring. The four identities of the pointwise operation lemma make every section function a ring homomorphism. Their naturality in site morphisms is that of f_A, so these homomorphisms define a morphism of ring sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: The underlying set-sheaf morphism is f_A, a composite of isomorphisms. Since sheafCompose of the forgetful functor from commutative rings reflects isomorphisms, the ring-sheaf morphism is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Naturality of e_R rearranges to naturality of its inverse. Combine that equality with naturality of κ_A^ring to show the ring-sheaf components are natural in ring homomorphisms; faithfulness of the forgetful sheaf functor reduces this to the underlying equality. Use NatIso.ofComponents. The component formula holds by construction.

lean.statement: theorem constantRingComparisonAssembly {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D] (JC : GrothendieckTopology C) (JD : GrothendieckTopology D) [HasWeakSheafify JC CommRingCat.{u}] [HasWeakSheafify JD CommRingCat.{u}] (L : Sheaf JC (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf JD (Type u)) (hL : PreservesFiniteLimits L) (rings : Sheaf JC CommRingCat.{u} ⥤ Sheaf JD CommRingCat.{u}) (e : ∀ R : Sheaf JC CommRingCat.{u}, RingInverseImage L R (rings.obj R)) (enat : ∀ {R S : Sheaf JC CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ S), L.map ((sheafCompose JC (forget CommRingCat)).map φ) ≫ (e S).ringUnderlying.hom = (e R).ringUnderlying.hom ≫ (sheafCompose JD (forget CommRingCat)).map (rings.map φ)) (kappa : constantSheaf JC (Type u) ⋙ L ≅ constantSheaf JD (Type u)) : ∃ (constants : constantSheaf JC CommRingCat.{u} ⋙ rings ≅ constantSheaf JD CommRingCat.{u}), ∀ A : CommRingCat.{u}, (sheafCompose JD (forget CommRingCat)).map ((constants.app A).hom) = (e ((constantSheaf JC CommRingCat.{u}).obj A)).ringUnderlying.inv ≫ ((constantRingSetComparison JC JD L kappa).app A).hom
